sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮

translations.literal: Tiegezhu
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu

sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮，高昌人。

translations.literal: Tiegezhu was a man of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu was a native of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 世居五城，後徙京師。

translations.literal: His family had long dwelt in Wucheng, and later moved to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived at Wucheng before relocating to the capital.

sentences.zh: 曾祖父達釋，有謀略，為國人所信服。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dashi was resourceful in counsel and was trusted by the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dashi was a man of strategic counsel whom the people of the realm trusted.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，高昌國主懼，以錦衣、白貂帽召達釋與謀。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor campaigned westward, the ruler of Gaochang was afraid, and summoned Dashi with brocade robes and a white sable cap to take counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched west, the king of Gaochang grew fearful and summoned Dashi for counsel, presenting him with brocade robes and a white sable cap.

sentences.zh: 達釋知天命有歸，勸其主執贄稱臣，以安其國，由是號為尚書。

translations.literal: Dashi knew that Heaven's mandate had found its destination, and urged his lord to present tribute and declare himself a subject, so as to secure the state; thereby he came to be styled Shangshu.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the mandate of Heaven had turned toward the Mongols, Dashi urged his lord to submit with tribute and become a vassal so the kingdom might be spared, and for this he was given the title Shangshu.

sentences.zh: 太祖班師，諸王言於帝曰：「達釋之子野里朮驍勇善戰，所將部落又強大。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor withdrew his army, the princes said to the emperor: "Dashi's son Yelizhu is fierce and brave in battle, and the tribes he leads are moreover powerful.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu withdrew his forces, the princes told the emperor, "Dashi's son Yelizhu is a fierce warrior, and the tribes under his command are strong as well.

sentences.zh: 聞其人每思率衆效順而未有機便，盍致之乎？

translations.literal: It is heard that this man often wishes to lead his followers in submission but has had no opportunity—why not bring him in?"
translations.idiomatic: We hear he has long wished to lead his people in submission but lacked the chance—should we not summon him?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖是其議，即詔給驛馬五百，迎與俱來。

translations.literal: " The Taizu Emperor approved this proposal, and immediately issued an edict granting five hundred relay horses to welcome him and bring him together with them.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu agreed, and at once ordered five hundred relay horses sent to escort Yelizhu to court.

sentences.zh: 既至，引見，甚器重之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was presented to the emperor, who greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived and was presented at court, the emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 丙午，太祖西征，野里朮別從親王按只台與敵戰有功，甚見親遇。

translations.literal: In the year bingwu (1246), when the Taizu Emperor campaigned westward, Yelizhu separately followed the prince Ajinai in fighting the enemy with merit, and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1246, during Taizu's western campaign, Yelizhu served under Prince Ajinai, distinguished himself in battle, and won exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 王方以絳蓋障日而坐，及聞野里朮議事，喜見顏色，稱善久之，既退，撒其蓋送之十里。

translations.literal: The prince was just then sitting with a crimson canopy shading the sun; when he heard Yelizhu discuss affairs, his face showed pleasure, and he praised him at length; when Yelizhu withdrew, he cast aside the canopy and escorted him ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had been sitting beneath a crimson canopy to block the sun; when Yelizhu joined the council, his face brightened and he praised him at length. When Yelizhu took his leave, the prince cast off the canopy and escorted him ten li.

sentences.zh: 遂得兼長四環衛之必闍赤。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was able concurrently to head the bichechi of the four ring guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed to head the imperial kitchen staff of all four ring guards.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，從國兵討金，以戰功最多，賞賚優渥。

translations.literal: In the year renchen (1232), he followed the national army in punishing Jin, and for the greatest battle merit received lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1232 he joined the campaign against Jin, earned the highest distinction in battle, and received generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 甲午，副忽都虎籍漢戶口，籌其賦役，分諸功臣以地，人服其敏。

translations.literal: In the year jiawu (1234), he assisted Huduhu in registering Han households, planning their taxes and corvée, and allotting land to the various meritorious subjects; people admired his efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: In 1234 he assisted Huduhu in registering Han households, assessing taxes and labor obligations, and distributing land among the meritorious officials—a work people admired for its swift competence.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮，野里朮長子也，尤沉鷙有才。

translations.literal: Tiegezhu was the eldest son of Yelizhu, and was especially deep, stern, and talented.
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu, Yelizhu's eldest son, was a man of exceptional reserve, force of character, and ability.

sentences.zh: 嘗有擁兵叛者，鐵哥朮率族人與戰于魚兒濼。

translations.literal: Once there was one who gathered troops in rebellion; Tiegezhu led his clansmen to fight him at Yuer Bulao.
translations.idiomatic: When a rebel raised armed followers, Tiegezhu led his kinsmen against him at Fish Lake Marsh.

sentences.zh: 時軍興，簿檄繁急，鐵哥朮一以其國書識之，無遺失者，帝甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: At that time the army was mobilized and documents and orders were urgent and numerous; Tiegezhu knew them all by his native script, with none lost, and the emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: During the mobilization, when orders and registers poured in, Tiegezhu could read every document in his native script without a single loss, and the emperor praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 至元中，擢為棣州達魯花赤，遷德安府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan era he was promoted to darughachi of Di Prefecture, and transferred to darughachi of De'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan reign he was promoted to darughachi of Di Prefecture and later transferred to De'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 適土人蔡知府者以衆叛，鐵哥朮率衆先登，冒矢石，身被數槍，猶戰不已，遂討平之。

translations.literal: It happened that a local man, Prefect Cai, rebelled with a crowd; Tiegezhu led the troops in scaling the walls first, braving arrows and stones, his body struck by several spears, yet still fighting without cease, and thus pacified the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When a local official, Prefect Cai, rose in rebellion with a mob, Tiegezhu led the assault over the walls, braving arrows and stones though pierced by several spears, and fought on until the revolt was crushed.

sentences.zh: 主將怒，將屠其城。

translations.literal: The commanding general was angry and was about to massacre the city.
translations.idiomatic: The commander, enraged, was about to slaughter the entire city.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥朮請曰：「叛者蔡知府數人而已，城中之人何預焉。

translations.literal: Tiegezhu pleaded: "The rebels are only Prefect Cai and a few others—what have the people in the city to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: Tiegezhu pleaded, "Only Prefect Cai and a handful of men rebelled—what crime have the townspeople committed?

sentences.zh: 盍誅其黨與而止，毋令濫及非辜。

translations.literal: Why not execute their accomplices and stop there, and not let punishment spread indiscriminately to the innocent?"
translations.idiomatic: Execute the ringleaders and their accomplices, but do not let punishment spill onto the innocent."

sentences.zh: 」主將嘉其誠懇，城遂得全。

translations.literal: " The commanding general commended his sincerity, and the city was thereby preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: " The commander was moved by his earnest plea, and the city was spared.

sentences.zh: 累官至嘉議大夫、婺州路達魯花赤，所在咸著政蹟。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Jiayi dafu and darughachi of Wuzhou Circuit, and wherever he served left notable records of governance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jiayi dafu and darughachi of Wuzhou Circuit, leaving a record of distinguished administration wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 大德己亥卒，成宗敕其孫海壽載其柩歸葬京師，贈榮祿大夫、江浙行省平章政事、柱國，封雲國公，諡簡肅。

translations.literal: He died in the year jihai of the Dade era; Emperor Chengzong ordered his grandson Haishou to convey his coffin back for burial in the capital, and posthumously conferred Ronglu dafu, Pingzhang zhengshi of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, Zhuguo, enfeoffed him as Duke of Yun, with the posthumous title Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1299. Chengzong ordered his grandson Haishou to bring his coffin home for burial in the capital and posthumously honored him as Ronglu dafu, Pingzhang of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and Zhuguo, enfeoffing him as Duke of Yun with the posthumous name Jiansu.

sentences.zh: 子四人：義堅亞禮，幼給事裕宗宮。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Yijianyali, who in youth served in the palace of the Heir Apparent Yuzong.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons. Yijianyali served in the household of Heir Apparent Yuzong from childhood.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年，為中書省宣使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan he became an envoy of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was appointed an envoy of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗使河南，適汴、鄭大疫，義堅亞禮命所在村郭搆室廬，備醫藥，以畜病者，由是軍民全活者衆。

translations.literal: Once he was sent to Henan; it happened that Bian and Zheng suffered a great epidemic, and Yijianyali ordered every village and hamlet to erect shelters, prepare medicines, and keep the sick, whereby many soldiers and civilians were wholly preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Henan, when Bian and Zheng were struck by plague, he ordered villages to erect shelters, stock medicines, and care for the sick, saving a great many soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 遷直省舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to attendant of the Direct Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the Direct Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 承中書檄徵考上都儲偫，及還，帝賜錦衣貂裘一襲，以旌其能。

translations.literal: He received a dispatch from the Central Secretariat to inspect and audit the reserves at Shangdu; when he returned, the emperor bestowed one set of brocade robes and a sable fur coat to honor his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched by the Central Secretariat to audit the reserves at Shangdu, he returned to receive brocade robes and a sable coat from the emperor in recognition of his competence.

sentences.zh: 出為湖州路達魯花赤，卒于官。

translations.literal: He went out as darughachi of Huzhou Circuit and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed darughachi of Huzhou Circuit and died in office.

sentences.zh: 月連朮，同知安陸府事。

translations.literal: Yuelianzhu was associate administrator of Anlu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuelianzhu served as associate administrator of Anlu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八扎，同知宣政院事。

translations.literal: Baza was associate administrator of the Xuanzheng Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Baza served as associate administrator of the Bureau of Buddhist and Tibetan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 孫九人，海壽，義堅亞禮子也。

translations.literal: He had nine grandsons; Haishou was the son of Yijianyali.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine grandsons. Haishou was Yijianyali's son.

sentences.zh: 由宿衛世祖朝累官至太中大夫、杭州路達魯花赤，招復流民有恩惠。

translations.literal: From palace guard service in the Shizu emperor's reign he rose through offices to Taizhong dafu and darughachi of Hangzhou Circuit, and in recalling displaced people showed benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from palace guard in Kublai's reign to Taizhong dafu and darughachi of Hangzhou, he won gratitude for bringing back displaced people with humane policies.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈翰林直學士，封范陽郡侯，諡惠敏。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously conferred Hanlin zhi xueshi, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang Commandery, with the posthumous title Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made Hanlin Academician, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang, with the posthumous name Huimin.

sentences.zh: 十年，改僉淮西等處行樞密院事，城正陽以扼淮海諸州兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to commissioner of the Huai-Xi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, and walled Zhengyang to choke off the troops of the Huai-Hai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1273) he was made commissioner of the Huai-Xi Branch Bureau of Military Affairs and built up Zhengyang to block Song forces along the Huai-Hai line.

sentences.zh: 宋陳奕率安豐、廬、壽等州兵數撓其役，塔出選精銳日十數戰，奕遁去，卒城正陽。

translations.literal: Song's Chen Yi led the troops of Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and other prefectures repeatedly to harass the work; Tachu selected crack troops and fought ten or more battles a day; Yi fled, and at last Zhengyang was walled.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi of Song led troops from Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and neighboring prefectures to harry the works repeatedly. Tachu picked elite troops and fought a dozen battles a day until Yi withdrew and Zhengyang was completed.

sentences.zh: 宋人復造戰艦於六安，欲攻正陽，塔出詢知之，率騎兵焚其艦。

translations.literal: The Song again built warships at Lu'an intending to attack Zhengyang; Tachu learned of it through inquiry and led cavalry to burn the ships.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song built warships at Lu'an to strike Zhengyang, Tachu learned of it and led cavalry to burn them.

sentences.zh: 餽饟久不繼，出兵據險，潛取安豐麥以餉軍，宋兵壁橫河口，塔出將奇兵大破之。

translations.literal: Provisions had long failed to arrive; he led troops to hold strategic ground, secretly took Anfeng wheat to feed the army; Song troops encamped at Henghekou, and Tachu led a surprise force and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies ran low, he seized strong points, secretly harvested Anfeng wheat to feed his men, and when Song forces camped at Henghekou, led a flanking force that routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 十一年，朝議：「淮上諸郡，宋之北藩，城堅兵精，攻之不可猝下，徒老我師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the court deliberated: "The prefectures along the Huai are Song's northern bulwark; their walls are strong and their troops skilled—an attack cannot bring them down at once, and will only weary our army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1274) the court debated: "The Huai prefectures are Song's northern rampart—strong walls and seasoned troops. They cannot be taken at a stroke, and a frontal assault would only exhaust our forces.

sentences.zh: 宜先渡江翦其根本，留兵淮甸絕其救援，則長江可乘虛而渡也。

translations.literal: It is fitting first to cross the Yangzi and cut their root, leaving troops in the Huai region to cut off their relief—then the Yangzi can be crossed while they are exposed."
translations.idiomatic: We should cross the Yangzi first and strike at the root, leaving forces in the Huai basin to block relief—then the great river can be crossed while the enemy is divided."

sentences.zh: 」於是以塔出為鎮國上將軍、淮西行省參知政事，帥師攻安豐、廬、壽等州，俘生口萬餘來獻，賜蒲萄酒二壺，仍以曹州官園為第宅，給城南閑田為牧地。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Tachu was made Zhenguo shangjiangjun and Canzhi zhengshi of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat, leading troops to attack Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and other prefectures; he captured more than ten thousand living captives and presented them; he was granted two jars of grape wine, and furthermore given the official garden of Cao Prefecture as a residence, with idle fields south of the city as pasture.
translations.idiomatic: " Tachu was appointed Zhenguo shangjiangjun and Vice Minister of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat and led attacks on Anfeng, Lu, Shou, and other prefectures. He sent more than ten thousand captives to court, received two jars of grape wine, was given the official garden at Cao Prefecture as his residence, and idle fields south of the city as pastureland.

sentences.zh: 宋夏貴帥舟師十萬圍正陽，決淮水灌城，幾陷，帝遣塔出往救之。

translations.literal: Song's Xia Gui led a fleet of a hundred thousand to besiege Zhengyang, breached the Huai to flood the city, and it nearly fell; the emperor sent Tachu to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui of Song led a fleet of one hundred thousand to besiege Zhengyang, breached the Huai to flood the city, and nearly took it. The emperor dispatched Tachu to the relief.

sentences.zh: 道出潁州，遇宋兵攻潁，戍卒僅數百人，盛暑，塔出即發公庫弓矢，驅市人出戰，預度潁之北關攻易破，乃急徙民入城伏兵以待。

translations.literal: On the road he passed through Ying Prefecture and encountered Song troops attacking Ying; the garrison had only several hundred men; in the height of summer Tachu at once issued bows and arrows from the public storehouse, drove townspeople out to fight, foresaw that Ying's north gate would be easy to attack and break, and urgently moved the people into the city and set ambush troops to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Ying Prefecture, he found Song forces attacking the city with only a few hundred defenders on hand. In the midsummer heat he issued arms from the public stores, pressed townspeople into battle, judged the north gate the weak point, evacuated civilians into the city, and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 是夜，宋人果焚北關，火光屬天，塔出率衆從暗中射之，矢下如雨，宋軍退走至沙河，大破之，溺死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: That night the Song indeed burned the north gate; firelight joined heaven; Tachu led the crowd to shoot from concealment; arrows fell like rain; the Song army retreated to Shahe and was utterly defeated; those drowned could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Song burned the north gate as he had foreseen, flames lighting the sky. Tachu rained arrows from ambush until the enemy fled to Shahe, where they were shattered; the drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 明日，長驅直走正陽，時方霖雨，突圍入城，遂堅壁不出。

translations.literal: The next day he drove straight to Zhengyang; it was then raining heavily; he broke through the encirclement and entered the city, and then held the walls and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he pressed on to Zhengyang through pouring rain, broke through the siege lines into the city, and held the walls without sallying forth.

sentences.zh: 俄復開霽，與右丞阿塔海分帥銳師以出，渡淮至中流，皆殊死戰，宋軍大潰，追數十里，斬首數千級，奪戰艦五百餘艘，遂解正陽之圍。

translations.literal: Soon the sky cleared again; he and Right Chancellor Atahai each led crack troops out, crossed the Huai to midstream, all fought to the death, the Song army was utterly routed, pursued for several tens of li, beheaded several thousand, seized more than five hundred warships, and thus lifted the siege of Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the weather cleared, he and Right Chancellor Atahai led elite troops out, crossed the Huai to midstream, and fought with desperate valor. The Song army collapsed; they pursued for miles, took thousands of heads and more than five hundred warships, and lifted the siege of Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 塔出乃上奏：「方事之殷，宜明賞罰，俾將士有所懲勸。

translations.literal: Tachu then memorialized: "While affairs are pressing, rewards and punishments should be made clear, so that officers and soldiers may have something by which to be admonished and encouraged."
translations.idiomatic: Tachu then memorialized: "With fighting at its height, rewards and punishments should be made explicit so officers and men know what to strive for and what to fear."

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，頒賞有差。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words and issued rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice and distributed rewards accordingly.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，淮西行省復為行院。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat was again made a Branch Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat was reorganized as a Branch Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 塔出引兵渡淮，屯廬、揚間。

translations.literal: Tachu led troops across the Huai and encamped between Lu and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Tachu crossed the Huai with his army and encamped between Luzhou and Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從丞相伯顏以舟師與宋軍戰，宋軍大潰，其臣賈似道奔揚州，遂分兵四出，克池州，取太平，順流東下，至建康、丹徒、江陰、常州，皆望風迎降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Chancellor Bayan with the fleet in battle against the Song army; the Song army was utterly routed; their minister Jia Sidao fled to Yangzhou; then they divided troops in four directions, took Chizhou, seized Taiping, went downstream eastward to Jiankang, Dantu, Jiangyin, and Changzhou—all submitted at sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he followed Chancellor Bayan's fleet against the Song. The Song forces collapsed, minister Jia Sidao fled to Yangzhou, and Mongol columns fanned out to take Chizhou and Taiping, then swept downstream through Jiankang, Dantu, Jiangyin, and Changzhou, each city surrendering at their approach.

sentences.zh: 時揚州未附，諜告揚州人將夜襲丹徒，守將乞援，塔出設伏以待，揚州軍果夜至，塔出扼西津邀擊之，殺獲溺死者甚衆。

translations.literal: At that time Yangzhou had not yet submitted; spies reported that Yangzhou men would night-assault Dantu; the defending general begged aid; Tachu set an ambush to wait; the Yangzhou army indeed came by night; Tachu held Xijin and intercepted them; killed, captured, and drowned were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou had not yet submitted when intelligence warned of a night attack on Dantu. The garrison commander begged for help; Tachu laid an ambush, and when Yangzhou troops came by night he blocked them at Xijin Ferry, killing and drowning a great many.

sentences.zh: 入朝，帝賜玉帶旌其功，授淮東左副都元帥，仍佩金虎符。

translations.literal: He entered court; the emperor bestowed a jade belt to honor his merit, appointed him Left Vice Commander-in-Chief of Huaidong, and he still wore the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor awarded him a jade belt for his achievements, appointed him Left Vice Commander-in-Chief of Huaidong, and confirmed his golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加通奉大夫、參知政事，領淮西行中書省事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was advanced to Tongfeng dafu and Canzhi zhengshi, and directed the affairs of the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he was promoted to Tongfeng dafu and Vice Minister, directing the Huai-Xi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時沿淮諸州新附，塔出禁侵掠，撫瘡痍，練士卒，備姦宄，境內帖然。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectures along the Huai had newly submitted; Tachu forbade plunder, soothed the wounds, drilled soldiers, guarded against treachery, and within the borders all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: With the Huai prefectures newly submitted, Tachu forbade looting, tended the war-ravaged populace, drilled his troops, and guarded against unrest until the region lay quiet.

sentences.zh: 俄遷江西都元帥，征廣東，塔出宣布恩信，所至溪峒納款，廣東遂平。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Jiangxi and campaigned in Guangdong; Tachu proclaimed grace and trust; wherever he went mountain passes and caves submitted allegiance, and Guangdong was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Commander-in-Chief of Jiangxi and marched on Guangdong. Proclaiming mercy and good faith, he won over every mountain pass and ravine until Guangdong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加賜雙虎符，為江西宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was additionally granted the double tiger tally and made Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he received the double tiger tally and was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 宋益王昰、廣王昺走保嶺海，復改江西宣慰司為行中書省，遷治贛州，授塔出資政大夫、中書右丞，行中書省事。

translations.literal: Song's Prince Yi Zhao and Prince Guang Zhao fled to hold the Lingnan coast; the Jiangxi Pacification Commission was again changed to a Branch Secretariat, the seat moved to Ganzhou, and Tachu was given Zizheng dafu, Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, directing Branch Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song princes Yi Zhao and Guang Zhao fled to the southern coast, Jiangxi was elevated to a Branch Secretariat with its seat at Ganzhou. Tachu was made Zizheng dafu and Right Chancellor, directing provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以二王事入議。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he entered court to deliberate on the affair of the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he went to court to discuss the campaign against the two Song princes.

sentences.zh: 帝命張弘範、李恒緫兵進討，塔出留後，以供軍費。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhang Hongfan and Li Heng to command troops in advance to attack; Tachu remained behind to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zhang Hongfan and Li Heng to lead the expedition while Tachu stayed behind to provision the army.

sentences.zh: 初江西甫定，帝命隳其城，塔出即表言：「豫章諸郡皆瀕江為城，霖潦泛溢，無城必至墊溺，隳之不便。

translations.literal: When Jiangxi had just been pacified, the emperor ordered the cities demolished; Tachu at once memorialized: "The prefectures of Yuzhang all build their cities along the river; when heavy rains flood and overflow, without walls they will surely be inundated and drowned—it is not convenient to demolish them."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi was first pacified, the court ordered its walls torn down. Tachu memorialized at once: "The Yuzhang prefectures all stand on the riverbanks. In flood season, without walls the people will be drowned—demolition would do more harm than good."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 降附之初，有謀畔者，既敗獲矣，塔出謂同僚曰：「撫治乖方之所致也，中間豈無詿誤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of submission there was one who plotted rebellion; once defeated he was captured; Tachu said to his colleagues: "This comes from misguided governance in soothing and ruling—among them how could there be no errors?"
translations.idiomatic: Early after the surrender, a rebel plot was crushed and the ringleaders captured. Tachu told his colleagues, "This stems from failures in our governance—surely some were misled rather than malicious."

sentences.zh: 」止誅其渠魁，盡釋餘黨。

translations.literal: " He stopped at executing the ringleaders and released all the rest of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: " He executed only the leaders and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 瑞州張公明愬左丞呂師夔謀為不軌，塔出廉知其誣，曰：「狂夫欲脅求貨耳，若以曚昧言遽聞之朝廷，則大獄茲興，連及無辜。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongming of Ruizhou accused Left Chancellor Lü Shiqiao of plotting sedition; Tachu through investigation knew it was false and said: "This madman only wants to extort goods by threat; if with vague words we hastily report to the court, then a great prosecution will arise and implicate the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongming of Ruizhou accused Vice Minister Lü Shiqiao of treason. Tachu investigated and found the charge false. "This madman only wants to extort money," he said. "If we report vague accusations to court, a great purge will follow and sweep up the innocent.

sentences.zh: 且師夔既居相職，詎肯為狂妄之事！

translations.literal: Moreover Shiqiao already holds a chancellorship—how could he be willing to do reckless things!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Shiqiao holds a chancellorship—would he commit such folly?

sentences.zh: 若遲疑不決，恐彼驚疑，反生異謀。

translations.literal: If we hesitate and do not decide, I fear he will be alarmed and suspicious, and contrary plans will arise."
translations.idiomatic: If we hesitate, he may grow alarmed and turn to desperate measures."

sentences.zh: 」乃斬公明而後聞，帝是之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beheaded Gongming and afterward reported it; the emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " He executed Gongming and then reported to court; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入覲，賜勞有加，復命行省於江西，尋以疾卒於京師，時年三十七。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he entered audience; additional rewards of consolation were granted; he was again ordered to the Branch Secretariat in Jiangxi; soon he died of illness in the capital at the age of thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In 1280 he attended court, received special honors, and was sent back to Jiangxi. He soon died of illness in the capital at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 妻明理氏，以貞節稱，旌其門閭。

translations.literal: His wife, of the Mingli clan, was famed for chastity and constancy, and her gate and lane were honored.
translations.idiomatic: His wife of the Mingli clan was renowned for her fidelity, and the court honored her household.

sentences.zh: 二子：長宰牙，襲爵中奉大夫、江西宣慰使；

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder Zaia, who inherited the rank of Zhongfeng dafu and Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons. The elder, Zaia, inherited the title of Zhongfeng dafu and Pacification Commissioner of Jiangxi;

sentences.zh: 次必宰牙，仕至征東行中書省左丞，妻伯牙倫，泰安郡武穆王孛魯歡之女，亦守義有賢行。

translations.literal: the younger Bizaiya, who served up to Left Chancellor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat; his wife Boyalun was the daughter of Prince Wumu Bolughuan of Tai'an Commandery, and she too kept faith and had worthy conduct.
translations.idiomatic: the younger Bizaiya rose to Left Chancellor of the Eastern Campaign Branch Secretariat. His wife Boyalun, daughter of Prince Wumu Bolughuan of Tai'an, was likewise noted for fidelity and virtue.

sentences.zh: 塔里赤

translations.literal: Talichi
translations.idiomatic: Talichi

sentences.zh: 塔里赤，康里人。

translations.literal: Talichi was a man of the Kangli.
translations.idiomatic: Talichi was a Kangli tribesman.

sentences.zh: 其父也里里白，太祖時以武功授帳前緫校，奉旨南徵至洛陽，得唐白樂天故址，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Yelilibai, in the Taizu era for military merit was appointed commander before the tent, and by imperial order campaigned south to Luoyang; he obtained the former site of Tang's Bai Juyi and thereupon made his home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yelilibai earned appointment as commander of the imperial guard in Taizu's reign for military merit. Campaigning south to Luoyang on imperial orders, he settled on the former estate of the Tang poet Bai Juyi and made it his home.

sentences.zh: 塔里赤幼穎異，好讀書，尤善騎射。

translations.literal: Talichi in youth was exceptionally clever, loved reading books, and was especially skilled in riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Talichi was precocious as a boy, loved books, and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 襲父職，參佐戎幕，調度軍馬，動合事宜。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post, assisted in the military camp, deployed and scheduled troops and horses, and in every move matched what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Inheriting his father's post, he served on campaign staffs, deploying cavalry and infantry with unfailing judgment.

sentences.zh: 行省奏充斷事官。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat memorialized to appoint him a judicial officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat recommended him as a judicial officer.

sentences.zh: 時南北民戶主客良賤雜糅，蒙古軍牧馬草地互相占據，命塔里赤至其地理之，軍民各得其所，由是世祖知其能。

translations.literal: At that time northern and southern civilian households, hosts and clients, good and base, were mixed together; Mongol army pasturelands for horse-herding and grasslands mutually encroached; Talichi was ordered to go to their lands and survey them; military and civilians each obtained their place; thereby Shizu knew his ability.
translations.idiomatic: With northern and southern households intermingled and Mongol grazing lands overlapping civilian holdings, Talichi was sent to survey the boundaries so soldiers and civilians each had their proper place. Kublai took note of his ability.

sentences.zh: 俾領蒙古軍圍樊襄，塔里赤躬冒矢石，所向摧陷，樊城破，襄陽降。

translations.literal: He was made to lead Mongol troops in besieging Fan and Xiang; Talichi personally braved arrows and stones; wherever he went he crushed and overthrew; Fancheng was taken and Xiangyang submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He led Mongol forces in the siege of Fan and Xiangyang, braving arrows and stones in person until Fancheng fell and Xiangyang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從丞相伯顏渡江，駐臨安，尋命平章奧魯赤等分為六路，追襲宋二王。

translations.literal: He followed Chancellor Bayan in crossing the Yangzi, encamped at Lin'an, and soon was ordered with Pingzhang Aoluchi and others to divide into six routes in pursuit of the two Song princes.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Chancellor Bayan across the Yangzi and encamped at Lin'an. Soon he and Pingzhang Aoluchi were ordered to divide into six columns in pursuit of the two Song princes.

sentences.zh: 塔里赤領軍至福建，所過秋毫無犯，降者如歸，宋都統陳宗榮率衆來降。

translations.literal: Talichi led troops to Fujian; wherever he passed not a hair was harmed; those who submitted were as if returning home; Song Commander Chen Zongrong led his crowd to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Talichi marched into Fujian without harming a soul; those who surrendered came as if returning home. Song Commander Chen Zongrong led his forces in submission.

sentences.zh: 以功遷福建招討使。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Fujian Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made Pacification Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時諸郡盜起，其最盛者陳吊眼，擁衆五萬，陷漳州。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in the various prefectures; the most powerful was Chen Diaoyan, who gathered a crowd of fifty thousand and took Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry broke out across the prefectures. The worst was Chen Diaoyan, who mustered fifty thousand men and seized Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行省承制命塔里赤為閩廣大都督、征南都元帥，緫四省軍，復漳州，生擒陳吊眼戮于市，餘黨悉伏誅。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat by provisional authority appointed Talichi Grand Commander of Min-Guang and Southern Campaign Commander-in-Chief, commanding the armies of four provinces; he recovered Zhangzhou, captured Chen Diaoyan alive and executed him in the market, and the rest of the faction all submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat appointed him Grand Commander of Fujian-Guangdong and Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Campaign with authority over four provinces. He retook Zhangzhou, captured Chen Diaoyan and executed him publicly, and put down the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 繼從征交趾，擊敗黃聖許等，積功加鎮國上將軍、三珠虎符、廣西兩江道宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: He then followed the campaign against Jiaozhi, defeated Huang Shengxu and others, and for accumulated merit was advanced to Zhenguo shangjiangjun, the three-pearl tiger tally, and Commander-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner of the Guangxi Liangjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He then campaigned in Annam, defeated Huang Shengxu and others, and for accumulated merit was promoted to Zhenguo shangjiangjun with the three-pearl tiger tally and made Commander-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner of the Guangxi Liangjiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 賀州盜起，塔里赤討平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in He Prefecture; Talichi suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in He Prefecture, Talichi suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 改福建宣慰使，又改浙東。

translations.literal: He was changed to Fujian Pacification Commissioner, and again changed to Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Fujian, then of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 金瘡發卒，贈輔國上將軍、浙東道宣慰使都元帥、護軍，追封臨安郡公。

translations.literal: An old wound reopened and he died; posthumously conferred Fuguo shangjiangjun, Commander-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner of the Zhedong Circuit, and Hugun; enfeoffed as Duke of Lin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An old battle wound reopened and he died. He was posthumously made Fuguo shangjiangjun, Commander-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner of Zhedong, and Hugun, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 子二人：脫脫木兒，邵武汀州新軍萬戶府達魯花赤；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Tuotuomu'er, darughachi of the Shaowu Tingzhou New Army Ten-thousand Household Office;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Tuotuomu'er, darughachi of the Shaowu Tingzhou New Army Ten-thousand Household Office;

sentences.zh: 萬奴，廣西宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: Wannu, Commander-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: and Wannu, Commander-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 塔海帖木兒

translations.literal: Tahai Temur
translations.idiomatic: Tahai Temur

sentences.zh: 塔海帖木兒，荅荅里帶人。

translations.literal: Tahai Temur was a man of Dadalidai.
translations.idiomatic: Tahai Temur was of the Dadalidai people.

sentences.zh: 其先在太祖時事國王木華黎，將左手大萬戶下蒙古軍，鎮太原以西八州。

translations.literal: His ancestors in the Taizu era served King Muqali, commanding the Mongol army under the Left Hand Great Ten-thousand Household, garrisoning the eight prefectures west of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears served Prince Muqali in Taizu's reign, commanding the Mongol forces of the Left Hand Great Ten-thousand Household and garrisoning the eight prefectures west of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 破金將王公佐軍，斬公佐。

translations.literal: They defeated the Jin general Wang Gongzuo's army and beheaded Gongzuo.
translations.idiomatic: They defeated the Jin general Wang Gongzuo's army and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 從攻陝右，征河西，滅金，皆有功，賜種田戶二百七十。

translations.literal: Following attacks on the right of Shaanxi, campaigning in Hexi, and destroying Jin, all had merit; they were granted two hundred and seventy farming households.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigns in western Shaanxi, Hexi, and the final conquest of Jin, they distinguished themselves and were granted two hundred and seventy farming households.

sentences.zh: 曾祖忒木勒哥嗣，從都元帥塔海紺卜征蜀，死於興元。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Temulege succeeded; following Commander-in-Chief Tahai Ganbu in campaigning in Shu, he died at Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Temulege succeeded to the post and followed Commander-in-Chief Tahai Ganbu in the Sichuan campaign, dying at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖扎剌帶嗣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhaladai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhaladai succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 扎剌帶卒，父拜荅兒尚幼，從祖扎里、荅朮相繼襲其職。

translations.literal: Zhaladai died; his father Baicha'er was still young; his uncles Zhali and Dashu in succession inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaladai died, his son Baicha'er was still a child, so his uncles Zhali and Dashu succeeded to the post in turn.

sentences.zh: 扎里從都元帥大荅征蜀，以所統軍二百人破宋軍于巴州，斬首三百級，生擒五十餘人。

translations.literal: Zhali followed Commander-in-Chief Dada in campaigning in Shu; with the two hundred men he commanded he defeated the Song army at Bazhou, beheaded three hundred, and captured alive more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhali followed Commander-in-Chief Dada in the Sichuan campaign. With two hundred men he routed the Song army at Bazhou, took three hundred heads, and captured more than fifty alive.

sentences.zh: 荅朮以西川行樞密院檄領兵三千人救碉門，大敗宋軍，斬首三百餘級，俘百餘人以歸。

translations.literal: Dashu by dispatch of the Western Sichuan Branch Bureau of Military Affairs led three thousand men to relieve Diaomen, utterly defeated the Song army, beheaded more than three hundred, and returned with more than a hundred captives.
translations.idiomatic: On orders from the Western Sichuan Branch Bureau, Dashu led three thousand men to relieve Diaomen, routed the Song army, took over three hundred heads, and returned with more than a hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 拜荅兒既長，始以父官從行省也速帶兒征建都，死軍中。

translations.literal: When Baicha'er had grown up, he first held his father's office and followed Branch Secretariat Yesudai'er in campaigning against Jiandu, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Baicha'er came of age he inherited his father's post and followed Yesudai'er of the Branch Secretariat in the campaign against Jiandu, dying in the field.

sentences.zh: 塔海帖木兒襲父職，初從行院忽敦圍嘉定，嘉定降。

translations.literal: Tahai Temur inherited his father's post; at first he followed the Branch Bureau Hudun in besieging Jiading, and Jiading submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tahai Temur inherited his father's post. He first followed the Branch Bureau under Hudun in the siege of Jiading until the city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進圍重慶，守將張珏出師迎敵，塔海帖木兒力戰陷陣，功最多。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Chongqing, the defending general Zhang Jue led troops out to meet the enemy; Tahai Temur fought fiercely into the enemy ranks and had the greatest merit.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to besiege Chongqing, he met defender Zhang Jue in battle, charged into the enemy lines, and won the greatest distinction.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又以都魯軍二百人破宋軍於白水江，奪戰船一，俘其衆十三人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, again with two hundred Dulu troops he defeated the Song army at Baishui River, seized one warship, and captured thirteen of their men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he again led two hundred Dulu troops to defeat the Song at Baishui River, capturing a warship and thirteen men.

sentences.zh: 陞宣武將軍、管軍緫管。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Xuanwu General and Commander-in-Chief of Troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Xuanwu General and Commander-in-Chief of Troops.

sentences.zh: 從也速荅兒征亦奚不薛，又從征都掌蠻，皆以為前鋒，殺獲甚衆。

translations.literal: He followed Yesuda'er in campaigning against Yixi Buxue, and again followed in campaigning against the Duzhang tribes; in both he served as vanguard and killed and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Yesuda'er against Yixi Buxue and the Duzhang tribes, serving as vanguard in both and taking a great toll of enemy lives and captives.

sentences.zh: 九溪蠻、散貓、大盤蠻尚木的世用等叛，從行省曲立吉思帥師往討，皆擒之，及殺其酋長頭狗等。

translations.literal: The Jiuxi tribes, Sanmao, the Dapan tribes, Shangmu, Shiyong, and others rebelled; he followed Branch Secretariat Qulijisi in commanding troops to suppress them, captured them all, and killed their chieftains Tougou and others.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiuxi, Sanmao, Dapan, and other tribes rebelled under leaders such as Shangmu and Shiyong, he followed Qulijisi of the Branch Secretariat to suppress them, capturing the rebels and executing chieftains including Tougou.

sentences.zh: 也速荅兒、藥剌罕率兵萬人會雲南兵討烏蒙蠻，至鬧竈，其酋長阿蒙率五百餘衆奔麻布蠻地，塔海帖木兒以四百人追至山箐中，大敗之，擒阿蒙以歸。

translations.literal: Yesuda'er and Yalahkan led ten thousand troops to join Yunnan forces in punishing the Wumeng tribes; reaching Naozao, their chieftain Ameng led more than five hundred to flee to Mabu tribal lands; Tahai Temur with four hundred pursued into the mountain ravines, utterly defeated them, and captured Ameng and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yesuda'er and Yalahkan led ten thousand men with Yunnan forces against the Wumeng tribes. At Naozao, chieftain Ameng fled with five hundred followers into Mabu territory. Tahai Temur pursued with four hundred men into the ravines, routed them, and brought Ameng back captive.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，又從也速荅兒西征，不知所終。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again followed Yesuda'er on the western campaign, and his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he again followed Yesuda'er on the western campaign, after which nothing more is recorded of him.

sentences.zh: 口兒吉

translations.literal: Kou'erji
translations.idiomatic: Kou'erji

sentences.zh: 忽都，蒙古兀羅帶氏。

translations.literal: Hudu, of the Mongol Ulodai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hudu was of the Mongol Ulodai clan.

sentences.zh: 父孛罕，事太祖，備宿衛。

translations.literal: His father Bohon served the Taizu Emperor and was on palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bohon served Taizu as a palace guardsman.

sentences.zh: 至太宗時為鎮西行省，領蒙古、漢軍從攻河中、潼關、河南，與拜只思、扎忽歹、阿思蘭攻秦鞏及仁和諸堡，又與拜只思守京兆。

translations.literal: In the Taizong era he was Western Pacification Commissioner, leading Mongol and Han troops in following attacks on Hezhong, Tongguan, and Henan; with Baizisi, Zhahudai, and Asilan he attacked the Qin-Gong and Renhe forts; again with Baizisi he defended Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he served as Western Pacification Commissioner, leading Mongol and Han forces against Hezhong, Tongguan, and Henan, and with Baizisi, Zhahudai, and Asilan captured the Qin-Gong and Renhe forts before joining Baizisi in the defense of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 歲乙未，授左手萬戶，從都元帥荅海鉗卜出征，卒軍中。

translations.literal: In the year yiwei he was appointed Left Hand Ten-thousand Household; following Commander-in-Chief Dahai Qianbu on campaign, he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year he was made Left Hand Ten-thousand Household and followed Commander-in-Chief Dahai Qianbu on campaign, dying in the field.

sentences.zh: 子扎忽帶，時在宿衛，弟忽都荅立襲其職。

translations.literal: His son Zhahudai was then on palace guard; his younger brother Hududali inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhahudai was then on palace guard, and his younger brother Hududali inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 忽都荅立卒，札忽帶嗣，為千戶，從行樞密院圍重慶。

translations.literal: Hududali died; Zhahudai succeeded, became a thousand-household, and followed the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs in besieging Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Hududali died, Zhahudai succeeded as thousand-household and joined the Branch Bureau in the siege of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 重慶守張珏遣勁兵數千出挑戰，札忽帶力戰大破之。

translations.literal: Chongqing's defender Zhang Jue sent several thousand crack troops out to challenge battle; Zhahudai fought fiercely and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Defender Zhang Jue sent several thousand elite troops to challenge him; Zhahudai fought fiercely and routed them.

sentences.zh: 回軍圍瀘州，未下，行樞密院遣入朝計事，授宣武將軍、管軍緫管。

translations.literal: Returning, the army besieged Luzhou but did not take it; the Branch Bureau of Military Affairs sent him to court to plan affairs; he was appointed Xuanwu General and Commander-in-Chief of Troops.
translations.idiomatic: The army then besieged Luzhou without success. The Branch Bureau sent him to court to report, and he was appointed Xuanwu General and Commander-in-Chief of Troops.

sentences.zh: 復還攻瀘，登城，與瀘兵搏戰而死。

translations.literal: He returned again to attack Lu, scaled the wall, and died fighting hand to hand with Lu troops.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to assault Luzhou, scaled the walls, and died fighting the garrison hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 子阿都赤嗣。

translations.literal: His son Aduchi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Aduchi succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 孛兒速

translations.literal: Bei'ersu
translations.idiomatic: Bei'ersu

sentences.zh: 孛兒速，脫脫忒氏。

translations.literal: Bei'ersu, of the Tuotuote clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bei'ersu was of the Tuotuote clan.

sentences.zh: 世祖時直宿衛，扈駕征哈剌章還，帝駐蹕高阜，見河北有駕舟而來者，顧謂左右曰：「是賊也，奈何？

translations.literal: In the Shizu era he was on direct palace guard; escorting the imperial carriage on the campaign against Hala Zhang and returning, the emperor halted on a high mound and saw north of the river someone coming in a boat, and turning said to those at his side: "That is a bandit—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: In Kublai's reign he served as a palace guardsman. Returning from the Hala Zhang campaign, the emperor halted on a high mound and saw someone rowing across the river northward. He turned to his attendants and said, "That is an enemy—what shall we do?

sentences.zh: 」孛兒速進曰：「臣請禦之。

translations.literal: " Bei'ersu advanced and said: "Your subject requests to repel them."
translations.idiomatic: " Bei'ersu stepped forward. "Let your subject meet them," he said.

sentences.zh: 」即解衣徑渡，揮戈刺死舟尾二人，拏其舟就岸，舟中之人倉惶失措，帝命左右悉擒之。

translations.literal: " He at once removed his clothes and crossed straight over, wielding his spear to stab dead the two men at the boat's stern, seized the boat to shore, and those in the boat were flustered and at a loss; the emperor ordered those at his side to capture them all.
translations.idiomatic: " Stripping off his coat, he swam across, killed the two men at the stern with his spear, dragged the boat to shore, and left its occupants in panic. The emperor ordered them all seized.

sentences.zh: 哈剌章平，以功論賞。

translations.literal: When Hala Zhang was pacified, rewards were allotted according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hala Zhang was pacified, he received rewards according to his merit.

sentences.zh: 子荅荅呵兒，從征孛可有功，由宿衛陞武德將軍、揭只揭烈溫千戶所達魯花赤。

translations.literal: His son Dada Ha'er followed the campaign against Boke with merit; from palace guard he was raised to Wude General and darughachi of the Jiezhijieliewen Ten-thousand Household Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dada Ha'er distinguished himself in the campaign against Boke and rose from palace guard to Wude General and darughachi of the Jiezhijieliewen Ten-thousand Household Office.

sentences.zh: 從征叛王乃顏、也不干等，奮戈擊死數人，擒也不干，收其所管欽察之民。

translations.literal: Following campaigns against the rebel princes Nayan, Yebuqan, and others, he wielded his spear fiercely and struck dead several men, captured Yebuqan, and received the Qipchaq people under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against the rebel princes Nayan and Yebuqan, he killed several enemies in fierce combat, captured Yebuqan, and took charge of the Qipchaq people under his command.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，進懷遠大將軍、元帥，卒。

translations.literal: In the Wuzong era he was advanced to Huaiyuan General and Marshal, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong he was promoted to Huaiyuan General and Marshal, and died.

sentences.zh: 月舉連赤海牙

translations.literal: Yuejulianchihaiya
translations.idiomatic: Yuejulianchihaiya

sentences.zh: 月舉連赤海牙，畏兀兒人。

translations.literal: Yuejulianchihaiya was a Uighur.
translations.idiomatic: Yuejulianchihaiya was a Uighur.

sentences.zh: 從憲宗征釣魚山，奉命修麴藥以療師疫，賞白金五十兩。

translations.literal: He followed Xianzong in campaigning at Diaoyu Mountain, was ordered to prepare fermented medicines to treat the army's epidemic, and was rewarded with fifty taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Möngke in the campaign at Diaoyu Mountain, prepared fermented medicines to treat the army's epidemic, and was rewarded with fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 繼從太子滿哥都征雲南，戰數勝。

translations.literal: He then followed the Crown Prince Mangudai in campaigning in Yunnan and won several battles.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Crown Prince Mangudai in the Yunnan campaign and won several victories.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，火都暨荅離叛，領兵與討平之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Hodu and Dali rebelled; he led troops to join in suppressing and pacifying them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262, when Hodu and Dali rebelled, he led troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，佩虎符，為隴右河西道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he wore the tiger tally and became Surveillance Commissioner of the Longyou Hexi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he received the tiger tally and was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Longyou Hexi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 兀朗孫火石顏謀亂，從皇太子安西王往鎮之，皇太子賜以白金五十兩。

translations.literal: Wulangsun Huoshiyan plotted rebellion; he followed the Crown Prince, the Prince of Anxi, to go and pacify it; the Crown Prince bestowed fifty taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: When Wulangsun Huoshiyan plotted rebellion, he followed Crown Prince Anxi to suppress it and received fifty taels of silver from the prince.

sentences.zh: 十五年，與伯速帶平土魯，皇子復賜金衣腰帶金碗，且以其功聞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, with Bosudai he pacified the Tulu tribes; the prince again bestowed golden robes, a belt, and a golden bowl, and moreover reported his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he and Bosudai pacified the Tulu tribes. The prince again rewarded him with golden robes, a belt, and a golden bowl and reported his achievements to court.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進官嘉議大夫，仍居舊職。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced in office to Jiayi dafu while still holding his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Jiayi dafu while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 二十年，進中奉大夫、四川等處行中書省參知政事，尋以疾歸秦州。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was advanced to Zhongfeng dafu and Canzhi zhengshi of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat; soon he returned to Qin Prefecture because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Zhongfeng dafu and Vice Minister of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, but soon retired to Qin Prefecture due to illness.

sentences.zh: 大德八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Dade.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1304.

sentences.zh: 至順中，贈推忠宣力定遠功臣、資善大夫、陝西行省左丞、護軍，追封威寧郡公，諡襄靖。

translations.literal: In the Zhishun era he was posthumously conferred the merit title of Loyal and Far-reaching Merit Subject, Zishan dafu, Left Chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and Hugun; enfeoffed as Duke of Weining Commandery, with the posthumous title Xiangjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhishun era he was posthumously honored as a merit subject, Zishan dafu, Left Chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and Hugun, enfeoffed as Duke of Weining with the posthumous name Xiangjing.

sentences.zh: 阿荅赤

translations.literal: Adachi
translations.idiomatic: Adachi

sentences.zh: 阿荅赤，阿速氏。

translations.literal: Adachi, of the Alan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Adachi was of the Alan clan.

sentences.zh: 父昂和思，憲宗時佩虎符為萬戶。

translations.literal: His father Anghesi, in the Xianzong era wore the tiger tally as a ten-thousand household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anghesi held the tiger tally as a ten-thousand household under Möngke.

sentences.zh: 阿荅赤扈從憲宗南征，與敵兵戰于劍州，以功賞白銀。

translations.literal: Adachi escorted Xianzong on the southern campaign, fought enemy troops at Jian Prefecture, and for merit was rewarded with white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Adachi accompanied Möngke on the southern campaign, fought at Jian Prefecture, and was rewarded with silver for his merit.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥叛，從也兒怯等征之，有功。

translations.literal: When Ariq Böke rebelled, he followed Yeerqie and others in campaigning against him and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ariq Böke rebelled, he followed Yeerqie and others against him with distinction.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統三年，從征李璮，身二十餘戰，累功授金符千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong under Shizu he followed the campaign against Li Tan, personally fought in more than twenty battles, and for accumulated merit was granted the golden-tally thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 he joined the campaign against Li Tan, fought in more than twenty battles in person, and for accumulated merit was made a golden-tally thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏、平章阿朮之平江南也，阿荅赤皆在行中，著戰功，歿于陣，帝憐之，特賜鈔七十錠、白金五百兩，為葬具，仍賜鎮巢之民一千五百三十九戶，命其子伯荅兒襲職。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan and Pingzhang Azhu pacified Jiangnan, Adachi was in the column throughout, distinguished himself in battle, and died on the field; the emperor pitied him and specially bestowed seventy ingots of paper money and five hundred taels of white silver for funeral goods, and moreover granted the people of Zhenchao, one thousand five hundred thirty-nine households, ordering his son Bocha'er to inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Bayan and Pingzhang Azhu pacified the south, Adachi was with them throughout, distinguished himself in battle, and fell in the field. The emperor pitied him, granted seventy ingots of paper money and five hundred taels of silver for his funeral, allotted him 1,539 households at Zhenchao, and ordered his son Bocha'er to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 伯荅兒從別急列迷失北征，與瓮吉剌只兒瓦台戰于牙里伴朶之地，以功受上賞。

translations.literal: Bocha'er followed Bieji Lieimishi on the northern campaign, fought Onggirad Jirgatai at Yalibanduo, and for merit received the highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: Bocha'er followed Bieji Lieimishi on the northern campaign, defeated Onggirad Jirgatai at Yalibanduo, and received the highest reward.

sentences.zh: 尋進定遠大將軍、後衛都指揮使，兼右阿速衛事，將阿速軍往征別失八里，與敵兵累戰累捷。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Dingyuan General and Commander of the Rear Guard, and concurrently directed the Right Alan Guard; he led Alan troops to campaign in Beshbalik, fighting the enemy repeatedly with repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Dingyuan General and Commander of the Rear Guard, also directing the Right Alan Guard. Leading Alan troops against Beshbalik, he won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 樞密臣以其功聞，賞白金、貂裘、弓矢、鞍轡等，尋復以銀坐椅賜之。

translations.literal: A Bureau of Military Affairs official reported his merit; he was rewarded with white silver, sable fur coats, bows and arrows, saddles and bridles, and soon again bestowed a silver armchair.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs reported his achievements. He received silver, sable coats, bows, arrows, saddles, and bridles, and soon afterward a silver armchair as well.

sentences.zh: 明安，康里氏。

translations.literal: Ming An, of the Kangli clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming An was of the Kangli clan.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，世祖詔民之蕩析離居及僧道、漏籍諸色人不當差徭者萬餘人充貴赤，令明安領之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan the Shizu Emperor decreed that more than ten thousand people among those scattered and separated from their homes, monks and Daoists, and persons of various categories not registered for corvée who ought not bear labor obligations should fill the Keshi ranks, and ordered Ming An to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 Kublai decreed that more than ten thousand displaced persons, monks, Daoists, and others not liable for corvée should be enrolled as Keshi guards, with Ming An placed in command.

sentences.zh: 明安歲扈駕出入，克勤于事。

translations.literal: Ming An year by year escorted the imperial carriage in and out, and was diligent in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year Ming An attended the emperor on campaign and at court, diligent in every duty.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授定遠大將軍、中衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Dingyuan General and Commander of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed Dingyuan General and Commander of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，賜佩虎符，領貴赤軍北征。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted the tiger tally and led the Keshi army on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the tiger tally and led the Keshi on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 又明年，立貴赤親軍都指揮使司，命為本衛達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Again the next year the Keshi Imperial Guard Command was established, and he was ordered to be its darughachi.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that the Keshi Imperial Guard Command was established, and he was made its darughachi.

sentences.zh: 尋奉旨領蒙古軍八千北征，明年，至別失八剌哈思之地，與海都軍戰有功。

translations.literal: Soon by imperial order he led eight thousand Mongol troops on the northern campaign; the next year, reaching the land of Beshbalik, he fought Haidu's army with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to lead eight thousand Mongol troops north. The next year, reaching Beshbalik, he fought Haidu's forces with distinction.

sentences.zh: 二十六年冬十二月，別乞憐叛，劫取官站脫脫火孫塔剌海等，明安率衆追擊之，五戰五捷，悉還之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in the twenty-sixth year, Bieqiling rebelled and plundered the official relay station of Tuotuohuosun Talahai and others; Ming An led the crowd in pursuit, five battles and five victories, and returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the twenty-sixth year, Bieqiling rebelled and raided the relay station of Tuotuohuosun Talahai. Ming An pursued him, won five battles in succession, and recovered everything taken.

sentences.zh: 至杭海，強民闊闊台、撒兒塔台等率衆作亂，奪三站地，劫脫脫火孫，明安引兵又追擊之，却其軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Hanghai, powerful men Kuokuotai, Sa'ertatai, and others led crowds in revolt, seized three relay stations' lands, and plundered Tuotuohuosun; Ming An led troops again in pursuit and repelled their army.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanghai, strongmen Kuokuotai and Sa'ertatai rose in revolt, seized three relay stations, and robbed Tuotuohuosun. Ming An pursued again and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 二十七年秋七月，布四麻、當先別乞失、出春伯駙馬、兀者台、朶羅台、兀兒荅兒、塔里雅赤等掠四怯薛牛馬畜牧，及劫滅烈太子昔博赤并斡脫、布伯各投下民殆盡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the twenty-seventh year, Busima, Dangxian Bieqishi, Chuchunbo the imperial son-in-law, Wuzhetai, Duoluotai, Wu'erdai'er, Taliyachi, and others plundered the livestock of the four kheshig guards, and moreover raided Prince Mielie's son Xibochi and nearly all the people under the appanages of Otuo and Bubo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year, Busima, Dangxian Bieqishi, imperial son-in-law Chuchunbo, Wuzhetai, Duoluotai, Wu'erdai'er, Taliyachi, and others raided the kheshig herds and nearly wiped out the households of Prince Mielie's son Xibochi and the appanages of Otuo and Bubo.

sentences.zh: 明安將兵追擊于汪吉昔博赤之城，賊軍敗走，還所掠之民并獲其牛馬畜牧等以歸。

translations.literal: Ming An led troops in pursuit at Wangjixibochi's fort; the rebel army was defeated and fled; he returned the people they had plundered and moreover captured their cattle, horses, and livestock and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ming An pursued them to Wangjixibochi's fort, routed the rebels, restored the people they had seized, and recovered their herds.

sentences.zh: 時出伯、伯都所領軍乏食，奉旨以明安所獲畜牧濟之。

translations.literal: At that time the armies led by Chubo and Baidu lacked food; by imperial order the livestock Ming An had captured was used to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of Chubo and Baidu ran short of provisions, the court ordered Ming An's captured herds used to feed them.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以功陞定遠大將軍、貴赤親軍都指揮使司達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, for merit he was raised to Dingyuan General and darughachi of the Keshi Imperial Guard Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Dingyuan General and darughachi of the Keshi Imperial Guard Command for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 時別失八剌哈孫盜起，詔以兵討之，戰于別失八里禿兒古闍，有功，賊軍再合四千人於忽蘭兀孫，明安設方略與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose in Beshbalik; an edict ordered troops to suppress them; he fought at Beshbalik Turguchan with merit; the rebel army again gathered four thousand men at Hulanwusun; Ming An set strategy and fought, utterly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Beshbalik, he was ordered to suppress them and distinguished himself at Turguchan. When four thousand rebels regrouped at Hulanwusun, Ming An devised a plan and routed them.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，復將兵北征，與海都戰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade he again led troops on the northern campaign and fought Haidu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1298 he again led troops north and fought Haidu.

sentences.zh: 七年，歿于軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died in the field.

sentences.zh: 子曰帖哥台，曰孛蘭奚。

translations.literal: His sons were Tiegetai and Bolanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Tiegetai and Bolanxi.

sentences.zh: 孛蘭奚，昭武大將軍、中衛親軍都指揮使，積官銀青榮祿大夫、太尉。

translations.literal: Bolanxi was Zhaowu General and Commander of the Central Guard, and through accumulated offices reached Silver-Green Ronglu dafu and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Bolanxi was Zhaowu General and Commander of the Central Guard, rising through accumulated offices to Silver-Green Ronglu dafu and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子桑兀孫，中衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Sangwusun was Commander of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sangwusun became Commander of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 桑兀孫卒，弟乞荅海襲職。

translations.literal: Sangwusun died; his younger brother Qidahai inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangwusun died, his younger brother Qidahai succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 忽林失

translations.literal: Hulinshi
translations.idiomatic: Hulinshi

sentences.zh: 忽林失，八魯剌氏。

translations.literal: Hulinshi, of the Barulas clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hulinshi was of the Barulas clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖不魯罕罕劄，事太祖，從平諸國，充八魯剌思千戶，以其軍與太赤溫等戰，重傷墜馬，帝親勒兵救之，以功陞萬戶，賜黃金五十兩、白金五百兩，俾直宿衛。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Bulughan Hanja served the Taizu Emperor, followed in pacifying the various states, served as a Barulas thousand-household; with his army he fought Taichiwen and others, was severely wounded and fell from his horse, and the emperor personally drove troops to rescue him; for merit he was raised to ten-thousand household, granted fifty taels of gold and five hundred taels of white silver, and made to serve directly on palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Bulughan Hanja served Taizu in the conquest of the realm as a Barulas thousand-household. Fighting Taichiwen, he was gravely wounded and fell from his horse; the emperor personally led troops to rescue him. For this he was promoted to ten-thousand household, granted fifty taels of gold and five hundred of silver, and assigned to palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 祖許兒台，年十五能馳射賊，以勇略稱。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xu'ertai at age fifteen could gallop and shoot at bandits, and was famed for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xu'ertai could ride and shoot down bandits at fifteen and was famed for courage and resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 從定宗征欽察，為千戶。

translations.literal: He followed Dingzong in campaigning against the Qipchaq and became a thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ögedei in the Qipchaq campaign and became a thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 領兵下西番。

translations.literal: He led troops down into the western tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops into the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 從世祖伐宋，至亳州，與宋人迎敵，敗之。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu in attacking Song; reaching Bozhou, he met the Song in battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Kublai against the Song, met the enemy at Bozhou, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 父瓮吉剌帶，初為軍器監官，從世祖親征阿里不哥，以功受上賞。

translations.literal: His father Onggiradai at first was an official of the Armory Directorate; he followed Shizu in personally campaigning against Ariq Böke and for merit received the highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: His father Onggiradai first served in the Armory Directorate, accompanied Kublai's personal campaign against Ariq Böke, and received the highest reward.

sentences.zh: 俄奉旨使西域，籍地產，悉得其實。

translations.literal: Soon by imperial order he was sent to the western regions to register land and produce, and fully obtained the truth of it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to the western regions on imperial orders to register land and produce, and reported with complete accuracy.

sentences.zh: 帝方欲大用之而卒。

translations.literal: The emperor was just about to employ him greatly when he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to give him greater responsibilities when he died.

sentences.zh: 忽林失初直宿衛。

translations.literal: Hulinshi at first served directly on palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hulinshi began as a palace guardsman.

sentences.zh: 後以千戶從征乃顏，馳馬奮戈，衝擊敵營，矢下如雨，身被三十三創。

translations.literal: Later as a thousand-household he followed the campaign against Nayan, galloped his horse and wielded his spear fiercely, charged the enemy camp, arrows fell like rain, and his body received thirty-three wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as a thousand-household, he campaigned against Nayan, charging the enemy camp at full gallop through a rain of arrows and sustaining thirty-three wounds.

sentences.zh: 成宗親督左右出其鏃，命醫療之，以其功聞。

translations.literal: Chengzong personally supervised those at his side in extracting the arrowheads, ordered him medically treated, and reported his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong personally supervised the removal of the arrowheads, ordered him treated, and reported his achievements to court.

sentences.zh: 世祖以克宋所得銀甕及金酒器等賜之，命領太府監。

translations.literal: Shizu with the silver urns and gold wine vessels obtained in conquering Song bestowed them on him and ordered him to head the Imperial Storehouse Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai rewarded him with silver urns and gold wine vessels taken in the conquest of Song and appointed him head of the Imperial Storehouse Directorate.

sentences.zh: 後以千戶從皇子闊闊出出征，還，留鎮軍中。

translations.literal: Later as a thousand-household he followed Prince Kuokuochu on campaign; returning, he was left to garrison the army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Prince Kuokuochu on campaign as a thousand-household and remained to garrison the army on his return.

sentences.zh: 後從成宗與海都、都瓦等戰有功，成宗嘉之，特命為翰林承旨，俄改萬戶。

translations.literal: Later he followed Chengzong in fighting Haidu, Duwa, and others with merit; Chengzong commended him and specially appointed him Hanlin Academician; soon he was changed to ten-thousand household.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought under Chengzong against Haidu and Duwa with distinction. Chengzong praised him, appointed him Hanlin Academician, and soon made him a ten-thousand household.

sentences.zh: 與叛王斡羅思、察八兒等戰，以功授榮祿大夫、司徒，賜銀印。

translations.literal: Fighting the rebel princes Oljei, Chabar, and others, for merit he was granted Ronglu dafu and Situ, and bestowed a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting the rebel princes Oljei and Chabar, he was made Ronglu dafu and Situ and granted a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 武宗嘗曰：「群臣中能為國宣力如忽林失者實鮮，其厚賚之。

translations.literal: Wuzong once said: "Among the ministers, those who can exert strength for the state like Hulinshi are truly few—reward him generously."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong once said, "Few among my ministers serve the state with the force Hulinshi does—reward him generously."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣使召見。

translations.literal: " Thereupon envoys were sent to summon him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: " Envoys were sent to summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 未幾武宗崩，仁宗即位，念其舊勳，賞賚特厚。

translations.literal: Before long Wuzong died; Renzong ascended the throne, recalled his old merit, and bestowed rewards especially generously.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could be received, Wuzong died and Renzong succeeded, remembering his old service and rewarding him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 失剌拔都兒

translations.literal: Shilabadouer
translations.idiomatic: Shilabadouer

sentences.zh: 失剌拔都兒，阿速氏。

translations.literal: Shilabadouer, of the Alan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shilabadouer was of the Alan clan.

sentences.zh: 父月魯達某，憲宗時領阿速十人入覲，充阿塔赤，從世祖至哈剌章之地，戰數勝，兀里羊哈台以其功聞，賜所俘人一口以賞之，後以金瘡發卒。

translations.literal: His father Yueludamou, in the Xianzong era led ten Alans to enter audience, served as atachi, followed Shizu to the land of Hala Zhang, won several battles; Uluyanghatai reported his merit, and he was granted one captured person as reward; later an old wound reopened and he died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yueludamou led ten Alans to court under Möngke, served as an imperial attendant, followed Kublai to Hala Zhang, won several battles, and was rewarded with a captive. He later died when an old wound reopened.

sentences.zh: 失剌拔都兒至自脫別之地，帝特賜白金、楮幣、牛馬等物。

translations.literal: Shilabadouer arrived from the land of Tuobie; the emperor specially bestowed white silver, paper currency, cattle, horses, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilabadouer returned from Tuobie, the emperor specially rewarded him with silver, paper currency, cattle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 至元二十一年，從丞相伯顏南征有功，仍充阿塔赤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan he followed Chancellor Bayan on the southern campaign with merit and still served as atachi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 he distinguished himself in Chancellor Bayan's southern campaign and continued to serve as an imperial attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗命放海青，曰：「能獲新者賞之。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered sea hawks released and said: "Whoever can obtain a new catch shall be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered his sea hawks flown and said, "Whoever brings back a fresh catch shall be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 」失剌拔都兒即援弓射一兔二禽以獻，賞沙魚皮雜帶及貂裘，且命於尚乘寺為少卿、於阿速為千戶。

translations.literal: " Shilabadouer at once drew his bow and shot one rabbit and two birds to present; he was rewarded with a shark-skin mixed belt and a sable coat, and moreover ordered as Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Directorate and as a thousand-household among the Alans.
translations.idiomatic: " Shilabadouer immediately shot a rabbit and two birds and presented them. He received a shark-skin belt and a sable coat, and was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Directorate and Alan thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授武略將軍，管阿速軍千戶，賜金符。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Wulue General, commanded the Alan army thousand-household, and granted the golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was made Wulue General, placed in command of an Alan thousand-household, and granted the golden tally.

sentences.zh: 乃顏叛，從諸王和元魯往征之，力戰有功。

translations.literal: When Nayan rebelled, he followed the princes Heyuanlu to campaign against him, fought fiercely, and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Nayan rebelled, he followed Prince Heyuanlu against him and distinguished himself in fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 乃顏平，帝賞以金腰帶及銀交床等。

translations.literal: When Nayan was pacified, the emperor rewarded him with a golden belt and a silver folding bed, among other things.
translations.idiomatic: After Nayan's defeat, the emperor rewarded him with a golden belt, a silver folding bed, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，進武德將軍、尚乘寺少卿，兼阿速千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was advanced to Wude General and Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Directorate, and concurrently Alan thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Wude General and Vice Director of the Imperial Transport Directorate while retaining his Alan thousand-household post.

sentences.zh: 征哈荅安等，敗之，獲其駝馬等物。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Hada'an and others, he defeated them and seized their camels, horses, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Hada'an and others, he defeated them and seized their camels, horses, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 成宗嘉其功，以軍二千益之。

translations.literal: Chengzong commended his merit and increased his army by two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong praised his achievements and added two thousand men to his command.

sentences.zh: 討叛王脫脫，擒之，以功受賞。

translations.literal: Suppression of the rebel prince Tuotuo: he captured him and for merit received reward.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the rebel prince Tuotuo he captured him and was rewarded for his merit.

sentences.zh: 大德六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Dade.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1302.

sentences.zh: 子那海產，襲其職。

translations.literal: His son Nahai Chan succeeded to his post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nahai Chan succeeded to his post.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，進宣武將軍、右衛阿速親軍都指揮使，賜三珠虎符。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was advanced to Xuanwu General and Commander of the Right Guard Alan Imperial Guard, and granted the three-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 he was promoted to Xuanwu General and Commander of the Right Guard Alan Imperial Guard and received the three-pearl tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，覃加明威將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding he was broadly advanced to Mingwei General.
translations.idiomatic: In 1325 he was promoted to Mingwei General.

sentences.zh: 徹里，阿速氏。

translations.literal: Cheli, of the Alan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli was of the Alan clan.

sentences.zh: 父別吉八，在憲宗時從攻釣魚山，以功受賞。

translations.literal: His father Biejiba, in the Xianzong era followed in attacking Diaoyu Mountain and for merit received reward.
translations.idiomatic: His father Biejiba followed Möngke in the attack on Diaoyu Mountain and was rewarded for his merit.

sentences.zh: 徹里事世祖，充火兒赤。

translations.literal: Cheli served Shizu and filled the post of huor chi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli served Kublai as a kitchen attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征海都，奮戈擊其前鋒，官軍二人陷陣，掖而出之，以功受賞。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Haidu, he wielded his spear fiercely and struck their vanguard; two government soldiers fell into the ranks; he supported them and brought them out, and for merit received reward.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Haidu, he charged the enemy vanguard, rescued two soldiers who had fallen in the melee, and was rewarded for his merit.

sentences.zh: 後從征杭海，獲其牛馬畜牧，悉以給軍食。

translations.literal: Later he followed the campaign at Hanghai, seized their cattle, horses, and livestock, and all of it was used to supply army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning at Hanghai, he seized enemy herds and used them entirely to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賞鈔三千五百錠，仍以分賚士卒。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this and rewarded three thousand five hundred ingots of paper money, and moreover distributed gifts to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, granted 3,500 ingots of paper money, and shared the reward among his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 成宗時，盜據博落脫兒之地，命將兵討之，獲三千餘人，誅其酋長還。

translations.literal: In the Chengzong era bandits held the land of Boluotuo'er; he was ordered to lead troops to suppress them, captured more than three thousand, executed their chieftain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengzong, when bandits seized Boluotuo'er, he was ordered to suppress them, took more than three thousand captives, executed their chieftain, and returned.

sentences.zh: 奉命同客省使拔都兒等往八兒胡之地，以前所獲人口畜牧悉給其主。

translations.literal: By order he went with the Guest Reception Commissioner Badu'er and others to the land of Ba'erhu, and all the population and livestock previously captured were given to their owners.
translations.idiomatic: On orders he went with Guest Reception Commissioner Badu'er and others to Ba'erhu and restored all the people and livestock previously captured to their rightful owners.

sentences.zh: 軍還，帝特賜鈔一百錠。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor specially bestowed one hundred ingots of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, the emperor specially granted him one hundred ingots of paper money.

sentences.zh: 武宗居潛邸，亦以銀酒器賞之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong dwelt in the latent residence he also rewarded him with silver wine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Wuzong also rewarded him with silver wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，立左阿速衛，授本衛僉事，賜金符。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide the Left Alan Guard was established; he was appointed its commissioner and granted the golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 the Left Alan Guard was established; he was made its commissioner and granted the golden tally.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，從湘寧王北征，以功賜一珠虎符。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing he followed the Prince of Xiangning on the northern campaign and for merit was granted the one-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1313 he followed the Prince of Xiangning on the northern campaign and received the one-pearl tiger tally for his merit.

sentences.zh: 乞台，察台氏。

translations.literal: Qitai, of the Chatai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qitai was of the Chatai clan.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年為欽察衛百戶，從土土哈征叛王失烈吉及乃顏有功，賜金符，陞千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan he was a Qipchaq Guard hundred-household; following Totoq in campaigning against the rebel princes Shilieji and Nayan he had merit, was granted the golden tally, and raised to thousand-household.
